title: Separation and detection of D-/L-serine by conventional HPLC
author: Shikanai, Ikimura, et al.

For measurement, samples were derivatized by mixing with 4 mM OPA-NAC solution at a ratio of 4:1 and reacting for 150 s at room temperature. A portion (10−20 μL) of the reaction mixture was injected onto high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) with the electrochemical detector (ECD). D-serine, L-serine and glycine in the sample react with OPA-NAC solution, and form diastereomeric isoindole derivatives that are separable by reversed phase HPLC.

10 mmol/L L-serine/D-serine/glycine were prepared in 10 v/v% methanol and stored at -20°C or lower. Stock solution was diluted with 10 v/v% methanol to required concentration before use. All standard solutions were stored in plastic containers to prevent adsorption to glassware.

steps.title: Prepare chemical reagents
steps.instruction: Gather all analytical‑grade chemicals listed (phosphate salts, K2CO3, HCl, EDTA‑2Na, OPA, NAC, methanol, Tris, DAO, catalase, glycine, D‑serine, L‑serine) from the catalog numbers provided; keep them at room temperature unless otherwise noted.

steps.title: Prepare phosphate buffer solutions
steps.instruction: Make Solution A by dissolving 15.6 g NaH2PO4·2H2O in 1 000 mL water; make Solution B by dissolving 35.8 g Na2HPO4·12H2O in 1 000 mL water. Mix 1 000 mL of Solution A with 160 mL of Solution B to obtain 100 mmol/L phosphate buffer (pH 6.0).

steps.title: Prepare mobile phase
steps.instruction: Combine 820 mL of the 100 mmol/L phosphate buffer (pH 6.0) with 180 mL methanol (ratio 82:18) and add 1 mL of a 5 mg/mL EDTA‑2Na solution to give a final EDTA‑2Na concentration of 5 mg/L.

steps.title: Prepare OPA‑NAC derivatization reagent
steps.instruction: First make 10.5 mol/L carbonate buffer (pH 10) by dissolving 6.9 g K2CO3 in ~50 mL water, then add 10 mL 2 N HCl and bring volume to 100 mL with water. Prepare 20 mmol/L OPA‑NAC solution: dissolve 27 mg OPA in 1 mL ethanol, add 32.7 mg NAC and enough 0.5 mol/L carbonate buffer (pH 10) to reach 10 mL total. Dilute this 4‑fold with 0.5 mol/L carbonate buffer (pH 10) to obtain a 4 mmol/L OPA‑NAC solution (final working concentration 4 mM).

steps.title: Prepare amino‑acid standards
steps.instruction: Dissolve L‑serine, D‑serine, and glycine each to 10 mmol/L in 10 v/v% methanol; store aliquots at ≤ ‑20 °C in plastic containers. Dilute the stock with 10 v/v% methanol to the required concentrations immediately before use.

steps.title: Collect and dissect rat brain tissue
steps.instruction: Sacrifice the rat, remove the brain, and slice it on ice into 2 mm‑thick coronal sections using a brain slicer. Dissect the prefrontal cortex (medial PFC, 2.60–4.60 mm anterior to bregma) according to the atlas.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue in methanol
steps.instruction: Place the dissected tissue in 10 v/v% methanol at a volume equal to ten times the wet weight. Homogenize on ice with a Polytron PT1200E at full speed for three 10‑second bursts. Incubate the homogenate on ice for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifuge and filter homogenate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenate at 15 000 × g for 15 minutes at 4 °C. Transfer the supernatant through a 0.22 µm Millex‑GV filter into a clean tube.

steps.title: Dilute supernatant for analysis
steps.instruction: Aliquot the filtered supernatant and dilute it 50‑fold with 10 v/v% methanol before further processing.

steps.title: Optional D‑serine removal treatment
steps.instruction: For the removal experiment, dilute the diluted sample 10‑fold with 0.2 M Tris buffer (pH 8.3) that contains 4 U/mL D‑amino‑acid oxidase and 2 000 U/mL catalase. Incubate 30 minutes at room temperature, then filter through a 10 kDa ultrafiltration membrane.

steps.title: Derivatize samples with OPA‑NAC
steps.instruction: Mix each sample with the 4 mM OPA‑NAC solution at a volume ratio of 4 : 1 (sample : reagent). Allow the reaction to proceed for 150 seconds at room temperature.

steps.title: Inject derivatized sample into HPLC‑ECD
steps.instruction: Inject 10–20 µL of the reaction mixture onto the HPLC‑ECD system (EP‑300, flow 500 µL/min, column Eicompak EX‑3ODS, 4.6 mm × 100 mm, 3 µm, 30 °C). Use the mobile phase prepared above; the electrochemical detector is set to +600 mV vs. Ag/AgCl. Record chromatograms with the EPC‑500/PowerChrom 2.5 software.
